Name: True Mathematics - A Gangsta's Fairytale [V1]
Notes:
True Mathematics was a group that Sadler used to work with, where a previously recorded version of "A Gangsta's Fairytale" was done, but it was apparently bad and Sadler stated it was too goofy and never expected it would be picked.

"We had actually already recorded that with this group we worked with called True Mathematics. But they had done a pretty bad job on it, they stabbed it to death. I had put that music on the tape Chuck sent to Cube before he got to New York, but honestly I never thought he would pick it. It was too goofy."

Name: AmeriKKKa's Most Wanted [Album Alternate Mixes]
Notes:
Ice Cube said this in "The Making of AmeriKKKa's Most Wanted - Part 3", implying that every person would mix the songs and the ones that are on the record were the best ones.

"The record was mixed by everybody. Everybody mixed the song. So Chuck would mix "The N*gga Ya Love To Hate", then I would come in, me and [Sir] Jinx would mix "The N*gga Ya Love To Hate", then Keith Shockley and Hank Shockley would mix it, and you listen to all five mixes and the mix that was the best is the one that made the record."

Name: ??? [Scrapped Skits]
Notes:
Sir Jinx said that there were three skits/inserts used, but "The Drive-By" was the only one that made it, meaning two more were scrapped entirely.

"Those inserts aren’t easy to make—musical versions of visual stuff. We had three of those planned, but “The Drive-By” was the only one we used on that album."

Name: ??? [Album Fill-Ins]
Notes:
Sir Jinx said Ice Cube and Chuck D told others to do album fill-ins, many of which claimed to be offbeat because they didn't do them with the tracks themselves. Sir Jinx says he has the tape for them and his job was to align them on-beat.

"We didn’t bring no hype man with us to New York, so basically Cube and Chuck flew to LA one weekend and told J. Dee, T-Bone, Shorty and Robin Harris to do some fills on the album, vocal stuff to use in the background. If you listen close, you can hear that none of those are on-beat, because they didn’t do them with the tracks themselves. I still have the tape with all of those vocal parts on there. My job was to put them in the right places."
